outcome: massive transfusion (>=4 units packed red blood cells)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 184 deliveries that utilized either uterine balloon tamponade (UBT) or vacuum-induced hemorrhage control devices (VHD) at an urban safety-net hospital.
finding: While no difference in massive transfusion rates was observed, vacuum-induced hemorrhage control devices (VHD) were associated with lower quantitative blood loss (QBL), fewer transfusions, shorter device indwelling times, and lower device expulsion rates specifically in vaginal deliveries compared to uterine balloon tamponade (UBT).
mod_finding: In vaginal deliveries, VHD was associated with better outcomes (lower QBL, fewer transfusions, lower expulsion rates, and shorter indwelling times) compared to UBT, whereas no significant differences in these specific outcomes were noted in Cesarean deliveries, although VHD still showed shorter indwelling times for both delivery modes.
